intro: Convert miles to kilometers (or kilometres) accurately for road trips, running races, cycling logs, and international travel distances. Under the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement, 1 statute mile equals exactly 1.609344 kilometers—making one mile about 60.9% longer than one kilometer. Use this mile in km calculator to multiply any distance by 1.609344, or scan common route benchmarks from 0.5 mi to 2,500 mi below.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Statute Miles vs. Nautical Miles & Distance vs. Speed
items: Road odometers and highway signs use the international statute mile (1 mi = 1.609344 km), whereas marine and aviation navigation use the nautical mile (1 nmi = 1.852 km exact, about 15% longer).
Do not confuse miles-to-kilometers distance with miles-per-hour speed (mph to km/h); although both share the 1.609344 multiplier, speed measures distance traveled per hour.

faqs.question: How many kilometers are in 1 mile?
faqs.answer: 1 statute mile equals exactly 1.609344 kilometers (about 1.61 km). Conversely, 1 kilometer equals approximately 0.62137 miles.

faqs.question: How does a mile compare versus a kilometer?
faqs.answer: A statute mile is 60.93% longer than a kilometer: 1 mile equals 1.609344 km, whereas 1 km is roughly 0.621 miles (just under two-thirds of a mile).

faqs.question: How do I convert from mile to km?
faqs.answer: Multiply miles by 1.609344 (km = mi × 1.609344). For example, 270 miles × 1.609344 = 434.52288 km.

faqs.question: Is a statute mile the same as a nautical mile?
faqs.answer: No. Land distances use the statute mile (1.609344 km), while maritime and aviation routes use the nautical mile (1.852 km exact).
